description: Issue #839: at RUN TIME a profile keyword is a built-in name unconditionally. Whether a name may be DECLARED is fixed by the language version, never by the profile set: `spec/grammar.md:408` says "a name that could be declared in one implementation but not in another would be invisible and unpredictable to a learner", so the declaration-slot guard must not be gated on a profile — measured, `define ask` raises `ol-reserved-word` under a Core-Language-only set exactly as it does under this fixture's set, and the Core-only side is pinned by `core-language/check/reserved-word-profile-names-under-core-alone`. So `define ask` halts at phase-1 registration with `ol-reserved-word` and the `ask` call on line 4 never runs. A corpus that checks a rule at one stage does not cover it at the other — keep an executing case for any rule both stages implement. `check()` and `execute()` reach that answer through one predicate, `@openlogo/parser`'s `isBuiltInName`, rather than composing it each; `packages/parser/src/built-in-names.test.mjs` pins the check side. Issue #1156 corrected the reason this description used to give, which denied that a run has any profile set of its own and claimed the primitives of all profiles ran regardless — false in both halves: the profile set is caller-supplied and is a property of the run (`ExecuteOptions.profiles`, `spec/execution-model.md:673-680`, "One value MUST govern both the check and the run"), and the run obeys it rather than executing primitives outside it (`execute-internal.ts` refuses a call outside the run's claimed set; measured before that guard, `forward 10` under a Core-only set was reported unknown and still moved and drew). The `ol-reserved-word` below is the profile-independent one; the `ol-bad-token` on line 4 is not — measured, it appears under this fixture's declared set but NOT under Core alone, which is why that set is declared. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`. The other findings recorded here are independent faults in the same program, each reported once.
